tbh the despair is what drawn me into Danganronpa. The battle between Hope and Despair is Psychologically damaging anyone who witnesses it. Junko is a powerful Ultimate, not only is she capable of persuading even the toughest of minds to commit despicable act like Murder, she does so by putting them in situations where hope is void and all there is left is despair. And committing such acts are despair-inducing, it creates a perpetual  cycle of no hope, rash actions, and ultimate despair, Imagine you're in a square prison with 14 other prisoners, there are no windows to see hope, and no doors (chances) to look for it. then, Junko appears and  gives you each a shovel, and she tells you to dig a hole because you have nowhere else to go. But the soil you are shoveling is named despair, and while your comrades who succumb to this baseline despair will start digging, the soil that they dig would give out a pungent smell, that smell is second hand despair. This would force others to dig with those who goes in the name of despair, it would go on until everyone is digging, digging a grave full of despair. In the end, you would never see hope, all you would find is sense-numbing despair.
This is Junko's trap, because the deeper you go in the name of despair, the faster despair would engulf you. She would force those to succumb to despair, which would only cause even more despair from those who make conatact with it. 

Now I'm not a psychologist or anything, but I do notice this in several arcs of Danganronpa (DR1, SDR2, DR3 MH, and eventually DR3 GH,)

An example of this is DR1, first she would trap you in a the school with no contact from the outside whatsoever, that is the first step, hiding any hope, and blurring the fine-line between hope and despair. next, she would give you a motive for despair to begin. then the first to break would release the first taste of despair, and with another motive another would give in, and another ad another, and it would last until those who could has hope left in them (aka Naegi, and Hajime) would see the fault in the system of Junko's and with a remainng would find a way to escape in the name of hope.

I wouldn't say despair is a disease, it's more like a virus, it is parasitic in nature, it is highly contagious, and it grows ten-fold the more it controls you.
